text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Yugoslavia continues to consistently implement the Dayton accord, the agreement on the Srem Baranja region and to promote relations with former Yugoslav republics and neighbouring states, says Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic.
- European Union Council urges acceptance of OSCE suggestions for resolving the problem regarding Serbian local elections.
- Serb organisations in Croatia say the Croatian government's letter of intention for peaceful reintegration of eastern Slavonia is on the whole acceptable but needs some additional clarifiations.
- Multinational Hong Kong company Surental will purchase a 60 percent stake in Centar, a Montenegrin department store chain. The firm will invest 1.9 million German marks in the purchase.
- Commercial banks are on the brink of insolvency, with barely 80 million dinars ($18.8 million) on bank accounts Monday as opposed to over 100 million dinars at the end of last week.
- Kosovo Liberation Army claims responsibility for the car bomb attack on Pristina rector Radivoje Papovic last week.
- Socialist Party of Serbia and Serbian Radical Party appeal against the decision of the Belgrade electoral commission which gave local elections victory to opposition colition Zajedno.

- Bosnian Serbs can calmly wait for the decision of the arbitrage on the northern town of Brcko, says director of economics institute Dusko Jaksic, who attended the talks on the disputed town in Rome.
- Opposition coalition Zajedno continues protests in Belgrade over annulment of local election results.
- Serbian Patriarch Pavle blesses student protesters who stayed up for the second night in front of a police cordon.
- Police beat and arrest student Zoran Trifkovic.

- Civic Alliance of Serbia calls on Serbian Radical Party (SRS) to cancel invitation to French National Front President Jean Marie Le-Pen to visit Zemun municipality. Le Pen is due to arrive on a three-day visit to Belgrade Tuesday as SRS guest.
